## Concept {.section-break}

<div class="section-kicker">Part 1</div>
<div class="section-title-text">Concepts of reproducible, AI-assisted project workflows</div>


## Motivation

::: {.motivation-layout}
<div class="motivation-copy">
<ul>
<li>Reproducibility is a hallmark of good science</li>
<li>A well-organized, reproducible project often makes work more efficient</li>
<li>AI-supported work is the <del>future</del> present</li>
</ul>
</div>

::: {.xkcd-figure}
![](./media/xkcd-replication-crisis.png){fig-alt="An XKCD comic about reproducibility and the replication crisis."}
<p class="figure-credit">xkcd.com · CC BY-NC 2.5</p>
:::
:::


## Problems with "standard" workflows

::: {.problems-layout}
::: {.simple-list}
<div><strong>Results drift from their code</strong><span>Copied tables and figures become hard to update or verify</span></div>
<div><strong>Files lose their roles</strong><span>Raw, processed, current, and obsolete versions become difficult to distinguish</span></div>
<div><strong>Decisions disappear</strong><span>Cleaning and modeling choices remain in memory or private conversations</span></div>
<div><strong>Sharing becomes risky</strong><span>Private data and unfinished material move into unsuitable places</span></div>
<div><strong>Reproducibility is hard</strong><span>Others (including your future self) will struggle reproducing your work</span></div>
:::

::: {.problem-figure}
![](./media/amiracleoccurs.gif){fig-alt="A black-and-white cartoon showing an unexplained step labeled 'Then a miracle occurs' in a mathematical derivation."}
<p class="figure-credit">Sidney Harris · ScienceCartoonsPlus.com</p>
:::
:::


## The ORDERly concept

<p class="figure-lead"><span class="w-org"><b>O</b>rganized</span> + <span class="w-rec"><b>R</b>ecorded</span> + <span class="w-doc"><b>D</b>ocumented</span> + <span class="w-exe"><b>E</b>xecutable</span> = <span class="w-rep"><b>R</b>eproducible</span></p>

::: {.flow-figure .orderly-flow}
<div class="flow-row">
<div class="w-org"><strong>Organized</strong><span>predictable<br>places</span></div>
<p>+</p>
<div class="w-rec"><strong>Recorded</strong><span>changes<br>and decisions</span></div>
<p>+</p>
<div class="w-doc"><strong>Documented</strong><span>purpose<br>and instructions</span></div>
<p>+</p>
<div class="w-exe"><strong>Executable</strong><span>saved steps<br>that run</span></div>
</div>
<div class="flow-down-arrow">↓</div>
<div class="flow-outcome w-rep"><strong>Reproducible</strong><span>a stated result can be recreated</span></div>
:::


## ORDERly AI work

<p class="figure-lead"><span class="w-org"><b>O</b>rganized</span> + <span class="w-res changed"><b>R</b>estricted</span> + <span class="w-doc"><b>D</b>ocumented</span> + <span class="w-eva changed"><b>E</b>valuated</span> = <span class="w-rep"><b>R</b>eproducible</span> AI support</p>

::: {.flow-figure .ai-flow}
<div class="flow-row">
<div class="w-org"><strong>Organized</strong><span>clear project<br>context</span></div>
<p>+</p>
<div class="w-res swapped"><strong>Restricted</strong><span>privacy and<br>scope limits</span></div>
<p>+</p>
<div class="w-doc"><strong>Documented</strong><span>instructions<br>and logs</span></div>
<p>+</p>
<div class="w-eva swapped"><strong>Evaluated</strong><span>checks before<br>acceptance</span></div>
</div>
<div class="flow-down-arrow">↓</div>
<div class="flow-outcome w-rep"><strong>Reproducible</strong><span>bounded, inspectable, and project-owned</span></div>
:::


## Implementation {.section-break}

<div class="section-kicker">Part 2</div>
<div class="section-title-text">Implementation</div>
<div class="section-subtitle">A setup to support an AI-assisted ORDERly workflow</div>


## An ORDERly project setup

<p class="figure-lead">The setup combines template structure, text-based tools, version tracking, AI guardrails, and a reproducible workflow</p>

::: {.orderly-spine}
<div class="w-org"><b>O</b><strong>Organized</strong><span>The template repository gives <code>data/</code>, <code>code/</code>, <code>results/</code>, <code>products/</code>, <code>assets/</code>, and <code>ai/</code> distinct roles</span></div>
<div class="w-rec"><b>R</b><strong>Recorded</strong><span>Git/GitHub history, generated outputs, AI-use logs, and project notes preserve the path taken</span></div>
<div class="w-doc"><b>D</b><strong>Documented</strong><span>Markdown, YAML, Quarto files, folder READMEs, and AI policy explain what to do and why</span></div>
<div class="w-exe"><b>E</b><strong>Executable</strong><span>Scripts and Quarto files regenerate processed data, analyses, figures, tables, and products</span></div>
<div class="w-rep"><b>R</b><strong>Reproducible</strong><span>An accepted result can be traced from input data through code to final communication</span></div>
:::


## Specific tools (largely interchangeable)

::: {.tool-matrix}
<div><strong>Editor/IDE</strong><span><b>Positron</b>, VS Code, RStudio, JupyterLab</span></div>
<div><strong>Coding language</strong><span><b>R</b>, Python, Julia</span></div>
<div><strong>Authoring</strong><span><b>Quarto</b>, Typst, R Markdown, Jupyter Book</span></div>
<div><strong>Tracking</strong><span><b>Git/GitHub</b>, GitLab, Bitbucket</span></div>
<div><strong>Agentic AI</strong><span><b>ChatGPT Codex</b>, Claude Code, Gemini CLI</span></div>
<div><strong>Workflow management (optional)</strong><span>renv, targets, Docker, Conda, Make</span></div>
:::


## The project structure gives each part a role

<p class="figure-lead">The main path moves through data, code, results, and products; support folders and root files provide stable inputs and guidance</p>

::: {.flow-figure .repository-flow}
<div class="flow-row primary-flow">
<div><strong>data/</strong><span>inputs<br>derived data</span></div>
<p>→</p>
<div><strong>code/</strong><span>workflow<br>stages</span></div>
<p>→</p>
<div><strong>results/</strong><span>generated<br>outputs</span></div>
<p>→</p>
<div><strong>products/</strong><span>deliverables<br>for audience</span></div>
</div>
<div class="support-row">
<div><strong>assets/</strong><span>stable<br>support</span></div>
<div><strong>ai/</strong><span>policy<br>summary<br>log</span></div>
<div><strong>root files</strong><span>readme.md<br>usage.md</span></div>
</div>
:::

::: {.work-tree-strip}
<span>work tree</span><code>data/</code><code>code/</code><code>results/</code><code>products/</code><code>assets/</code><code>ai/</code><code>readme.md</code><code>usage.md</code>
:::


## Separate raw, derived, private, and large data

::: {.data-layout}
::: {.simple-list}
<div><strong>raw-data/</strong><span>Original input; preserve it unchanged</span></div>
<div><strong>processed-data/</strong><span>Cleaned or transformed data generated by code</span></div>
<div><strong>private-data/</strong><span>Restricted material kept in an approved location</span></div>
<div><strong>large-files/</strong><span>Material too large for ordinary Git and GitHub use</span></div>
:::

::: {.data-figure}
![](./media/phd_dataisorare.gif){fig-alt="A PhD Comics cartoon about whether data is singular or plural."}
<p class="figure-credit">Jorge Cham · phdcomics.com</p>
:::
:::

::: {.work-tree-strip}
<span>work tree</span><code>data/raw-data/</code><code>data/processed-data/</code><code>data/private-data/</code><code>data/large-files/</code><code>data/readme-data.md</code>
:::


## Track changes with Git, guard what you share

::: {.git-layout}
<div class="git-copy">
<ul>
<li>Commit small, meaningful changes; push to back up and to share</li>
<li>Start <strong>private</strong>; go public later after checking data, outputs, license, and authorship</li>
<li>Once something is pushed, it is hard to remove from history — decide before you commit</li>
<li>Keep sensitive data out via <code>.gitignore</code>; <code>data/private-data/</code> is ignored by default</li>
<li>Nothing above roughly <strong>20 MB</strong>; use the ignored <code>large-files/</code> folders instead</li>
</ul>
</div>

::: {.xkcd-figure}
![](./media/xkcd-git.png){fig-alt="An XKCD comic in which someone explains that the way to use Git is to memorize shell commands and start over when errors appear."}
<p class="figure-credit">xkcd.com · CC BY-NC 2.5</p>
:::
:::


## Code follows the stages of the analysis

<p class="figure-lead">Each stage should have recognizable inputs, outputs, and instructions</p>

::: {.flow-figure .code-flow}
<div class="flow-row primary-flow">
<div><strong>data-processing</strong><span>raw to<br>processed</span></div>
<p>→</p>
<div><strong>data-exploration</strong><span>checks<br>summaries</span></div>
<p>→</p>
<div><strong>modeling-analysis</strong><span>models<br>results</span></div>
<p>→</p>
<div><strong>figures-tables</strong><span>final<br>outputs</span></div>
</div>
<div class="utility-strip"><strong>utilities/</strong><span>is optional support for repeated helper logic</span></div>
:::

::: {.work-tree-strip}
<span>work tree</span><code>code/data-processing/</code><code>code/data-exploration/</code><code>code/modeling-analysis/</code><code>code/figures-tables/</code><code>code/utilities/</code>
:::


## Keep generated outputs separate from everything else

::: {.simple-list}
<div><strong>results/</strong><span>Code-generated model objects, intermediate outputs, figures, and tables</span></div>
<div><strong>products/</strong><span>Reports, manuscripts, supplements, presentations, posters, and apps</span></div>
<div><strong>assets/</strong><span>References, PDFs, schematics, and other stable supporting material</span></div>
<div><strong>ai/</strong><span>AI policy, project context, guidance, and meaningful-use records</span></div>
:::

::: {.work-tree-strip}
<span>work tree</span><code>results/figures/</code><code>results/tables/</code><code>results/output/</code><code>products/report/</code><code>products/manuscript/</code><code>products/presentation/</code><code>assets/</code><code>ai/</code>
:::


## Running the workflow

::: {.run-order}
<div><span>1</span><code>code/data-processing/processing-code.r</code><em>writes <code>data/processed-data/</code></em></div>
<div><span>2</span><code>code/data-exploration/eda-code.r</code><em>writes <code>results/output/</code></em></div>
<div><span>3</span><code>code/modeling-analysis/statistical-analysis.r</code><em>writes <code>results/output/</code></em></div>
<div><span>4</span><code>code/figures-tables/make-tables.r</code><em>writes <code>results/tables/</code></em></div>
<div><span>5</span><code>code/figures-tables/make-figures.r</code><em>writes <code>results/figures/</code></em></div>
<div><span>6</span><b><code>quarto render</code> the products you need</b><em>writes <code>products/</code></em></div>
:::

::: {.rule-list}
<div>Steps 4 and 5 may run in either order, but both come after steps 1–3</div>
<div>Never hand-edit raw data, generated tables, or figures — change the code and rerun</div>
:::

<p class="closing-line">Regenerate results before updating the products that use them</p>


## The template ships a working example

<p class="figure-lead">Run it end to end once, then replace it piece by piece with your own project</p>

::: {.example-grid}
<div><strong>Data and code</strong><span><code>data/raw-data/example-data.xlsx</code> and five short R scripts, one per workflow stage</span></div>
<div><strong>Generated results</strong><span><code>results/output/</code>, <code>results/tables/</code>, and <code>results/figures/</code>, all rebuilt from code</span></div>
<div><strong>Finished products</strong><span><code>report.qmd</code>, <code>manuscript.qmd</code> with supplement, an example presentation, and a poster stub</span></div>
:::

<p class="closing-line">Every number and figure in those products can be traced back to a script</p>


## AI can support project work

::: {.ai-support-grid}
<div><strong>Code</strong><span>Write, document, refactor, and debug project code</span></div>
<div><strong>Literature</strong><span>Help search, summarize, and organize background material</span></div>
<div><strong>Writing</strong><span>Draft or improve reports, manuscripts, and presentations</span></div>
<div><strong>Documentation</strong><span>Keep code, outputs, and documentation aligned</span></div>
:::


## How AI plugs into this project

::: {.simple-list}
<div><strong>Run it inside the repository</strong><span>Use an agentic tool that can read and write project files and run code</span></div>
<div><strong>Point it at the documents first</strong><span><code>readme.md</code>, <code>usage.md</code>, <code>agents.md</code>, and <code>code-guidelines.md</code> carry the project rules</span></div>
<div><strong>Bound what it may do</strong><span><code>ai/ai-use-policy.md</code> states what AI may touch, and what must never leave the project</span></div>
<div><strong>Let it record its work</strong><span><code>ai/ai-use-log.md</code> is written by the AI; <code>ai/project-summary.yml</code> keeps it oriented</span></div>
<div><strong>Keep changes reviewable</strong><span>Ask for small steps, then rerun affected scripts and re-render affected products</span></div>
:::

::: {.work-tree-strip}
<span>work tree</span><code>agents.md</code><code>code-guidelines.md</code><code>ai/ai-use-policy.md</code><code>ai/ai-use-log.md</code><code>ai/project-summary.yml</code>
:::




## AI can support ORDERly habits

<p class="figure-lead">Things worth asking your assistant to do</p>

::: {.ai-asks}
<div class="w-org"><strong>Organized</strong><em>"Check that every file sits in the folder its role calls for."</em></div>
<div class="w-rec"><strong>Recorded</strong><em>"Summarize what changed today and why, and log your own contribution."</em></div>
<div class="w-doc"><strong>Documented</strong><em>"Update the READMEs and usage notes to match what the code now does."</em></div>
<div class="w-exe"><strong>Executable</strong><em>"Run this script in a clean session and fix what breaks."</em></div>
<div class="w-rep"><strong>Reproducible</strong><em>"Trace this figure back to the data it came from and show me the path."</em></div>
:::


## An ORDERly project is easy to work with

::: {.closing-composition}
<p><strong>Current you</strong> can work efficiently</p>
<p><strong>Future you</strong> can recover the reasoning</p>
<p><strong>Collaborators</strong> can inspect and extend the work</p>
<p><strong>AI</strong> can assist appropriately</p>
<p><strong>Others</strong> can understand and recreate the stated result</p>
:::
